references.text: God predicts that the Israelites will receive favor from the Egyptians and will ask for silver and gold articles and clothing, which is fulfilled in Exodus 12:36.
Moses is told that the people should ask the Egyptians for silver and gold articles, and that the Lord will grant them favor with the Egyptians.
God's promise to Abraham that his descendants would leave slavery with great wealth, fulfilled when the Israelites depart Egypt carrying the Egyptians' possessions.
The psalm describes how God led Israel out with silver and gold, a poetic retelling of the event in Exodus 12:36.
The gold and silver that the Israelites received from the Egyptians were later used as offerings for building the tabernacle.
Unfortunately, the gold jewelry the people received from the Egyptians was also used to make the golden calf.
Sources referring to the same event; verse 11:3 is the promise of favor, which Exodus 12:36 shows has been fulfilled.
Theological parallel: God's exaltation of His people by enriching them at the expense of their enemies during the exodus.
Direct fulfillment of prophecy; 3:21 is the promise, and 12:36 is its fulfillment.
